details:
Exploring the Science and Challenges of Living Beyond Earth

Project Overview

It is a first-person, 3D educational simulation game that allows students to explore, operate, and manage extraterrestrial settlements on Mars and the Moon.

Players experience the challenges of establishing and sustaining human outposts beyond Earth by managing crew activities, essential resources, interconnected life-support systems, power supplies, and responding to environmental and operational hazards.

The primary objective is to make space science engaging, interactive, and accessible. Instead of simply reading about space exploration, students learn by experiencing realistic situations, making decisions, solving problems, and understanding the scientific principles behind humanity's future in space.

Science-Based Learning, Not Science Fiction

Unlike conventional fictional space games, this project places real scientific knowledge and established space exploration concepts at the centre of gameplay.

The environments, challenges, resource-management systems, and operational scenarios are designed around scientifically grounded concepts. The objective is to help students understand the difference between scientific possibilities, current technological capabilities, and fictional representations of space.

Players do not simply explore planets for entertainment. They learn about the science, engineering, technology, and decision-making required to establish sustainable human settlements beyond Earth.

The game transforms complex space science concepts into understandable and enjoyable learning experiences. Students acquire knowledge naturally through exploration, experimentation, observation, and problem-solving.

Interactive Learning Through Realistic Consequences

Learning is integrated directly into gameplay. Every important decision can have consequences for the outpost and its crew.

Players must understand and manage interconnected systems involving:

  • Oxygen supply and life-support systems.
  • Water availability and conservation.
  • Food supplies and crew requirements.
  • Electrical power generation and energy storage.
  • Solar energy availability during planetary and lunar day-night cycles.
  • Environmental hazards and space-weather events.
  • Crew safety, operational priorities, and emergency responses.

Poor decisions can affect multiple systems. For example, inadequate energy management can compromise essential life-support operations, while failure to respond to environmental hazards can threaten crew safety.

This approach encourages critical thinking, resource management, scientific reasoning, and an understanding of how different technologies and systems depend on one another.

Accessible and Progressive Gameplay

The game is designed to accommodate students with different levels of gaming experience and scientific knowledge through three gameplay modes:

1. Demo Mode

Introduces players to the outpost environment, basic controls, major systems, and fundamental concepts. It provides an easy starting point for first-time players and demonstrations.

2. Practice Mode

Allows players to experiment, explore, make decisions, and develop their skills in a less demanding environment. Students can learn from mistakes and understand how different systems interact.

3. Real Mode

Challenges players to apply their knowledge in more realistic operational scenarios, where resource constraints, environmental conditions, system dependencies, and crew safety become important considerations.

Accessible Technology and Performance

The project uses moderately sophisticated 3D graphics rather than demanding, high-end visual effects.

This is a deliberate design decision to prioritize accessibility and performance. The objective is to make the game playable on ordinary computers without requiring expensive gaming hardware or advanced graphics capabilities.

By balancing visual quality and system requirements, the project aims to make interactive space science education accessible to a wider range of students.

Integration of Real-Time Space Science Data

An important aspect of the project is its potential to incorporate real-world space science data into the simulation.

For example, NASA's DONKI (Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information) API can provide information about actual space-weather events, including solar flares and coronal mass ejections.

Such data can be used to introduce real-world events as dynamic simulation scenarios. Players could experience how a space-weather event affects an outpost and learn why astronauts, equipment, communications, and power systems may require protection.

This creates a meaningful connection between simulated gameplay and actual space science observations.

Rather than learning about space events only from textbooks, students can explore their implications through interactive scenarios based on real scientific information.

Future Development and Expansion

This project is an evolving educational platform with several opportunities for further development.

Future improvements will focus on:

  • Expanding Mars and Lunar environments and introducing additional scientifically grounded scenarios.
  • Developing more sophisticated crew, resource, life-support, and emergency-management systems.
  • Integrating additional real-time data from NASA and other reliable space science sources.
  • Introducing more interactive scientific experiments and educational challenges.
  • Improving gameplay, graphics, and simulation capabilities.
  • Making the game installable and accessible on mobile phones, tablets, and other computing devices.
  • Reaching a wider student audience through accessible hardware requirements and progressive learning experiences.

Our Vision

Our vision is to make space science accessible, understandable, and exciting for students by allowing them to experience the challenges of living and working beyond Earth.

This is not just a game about exploring space; it is a game about understanding the science, technology, engineering, and decisions that will make humanity's future in space possible.
